market_summary: Markets are mixed with the Dow closing above 50,000 while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined today, with SPY down 0.29% and QQQ down 0.65%. NVDA gave back 3.91% today after yesterday's historic 31% surge as board scrutiny headlines weigh on sentiment. Extreme Fear persists with VIX at 28.29 and the Fear & Greed Index at 11.
key_insight: Nvidia board governance headlines and Microsoft cloud outage news are pressuring mega-cap tech, while elevated VIX and Extreme Fear readings suggest potential for further volatility ahead of MRVL, CRM, and SNOW earnings next week.
sentiment_commentary: The Fear & Greed Index at 11 (Extreme Fear) represents historically rare pessimism levels that often precede intermediate-term bottoms, but can persist during genuine drawdowns. With VIX at 28.29 and rising, the market is pricing in continued uncertainty around tech governance and macro headwinds, favoring hedged or volatility-long positioning in the near term.
notable_movers: NVDA dropped 3.91% today as AP News and Politico reported scrutiny of Jensen Huang's board reinstatement, partially reversing yesterday's massive rally. UVIX surged 8.45% today reflecting rising volatility demand, while SLV gained 0.71% as safe-haven flows continue. OTLY was the standout gainer at +26.12% today on what appears to be a momentum breakout.
macro_context: The 10-Year Treasury at 4.91% continues to pressure equity valuations, with the yield curve spread at 0.28% suggesting normalized but tight conditions. GDP growth at 4.3% remains strong but unemployment at 4.1% and the Fed Funds rate at 3.88% signal the Fed is in no rush to cut further. The bearish sentiment spread of -37% with 55% bears reflects deep pessimism that could either validate further downside or set up a contrarian bounce.

swing_trades.thesis: UVIX up 8.45% today with VIX at 28.29 and Extreme Fear at 11. Our prior UVIX trades hit +36.62% and +23.85% targets in similar setups. Tech governance headlines (NVDA board scrutiny, MSFT cloud outage) plus heavy earnings week (CRM, SNOW, MRVL) provide catalysts for continued vol expansion. UVIX shows strong momentum when fear readings are sub-15 and VIX is trending above 25.
swing_trades.invalidation: If VIX drops below 24 and SPY reclaims $725, the vol trade is cancelled as fear subsides.

swing_trades.volume_signal: High volume, inverse Nasdaq demand rising
swing_trades.thesis: SQQQ gained 1.93% today as QQQ fell 0.65%, with NVDA down 3.91%, MSFT down 1.25%, and GOOGL down 2.13% showing broad mega-cap weakness. Our prior SQQQ trade hit target for +23.85% in 3 days. Heavy tech earnings next week (CRM, SNOW, MRVL) create binary risk events likely to pressure QQQ. SQQQ shows relative strength vs SPY-inverse plays given tech-specific headwinds from governance and cloud outage narratives.
swing_trades.invalidation: If QQQ reclaims $645 with strong breadth and VIX drops below 24, the bearish Nasdaq thesis is invalidated.

Hold with current stop; this mirrors the prior winning SQQQ setup and has room to run toward $56.

The catalyst pipeline is strong with CRM/SNOW/MRVL earnings, ongoing NVDA governance scrutiny, and MSFT cloud outage fallout.
